summary: Pierce County ski-area summit; the register and firelookout.com list a 1934 NPS cab gone by the 1970s, but a 2016 visit doubts it existed, and comms gear sits there now.

facts.design: National Park Service cab, listed by firelookout.org as a two-story cab
facts.status_note: Register and firelookout.com say the cab was gone in the 1970s. Willhite, who visited in 2016, does not believe a lookout existed here.

access.note: The summit sits within the Crystal Mountain ski area. Willhite's route is the summer gondola to the ridge, then a walk to the high point north of the Summit House. He says the gondola route works in summer, which is the basis for 'restricted' (seasonal). No source states the resort's access policy.

visit.trail_note: No tower stands here. Willhite says that in summer you can take the gondola to the ridge and walk to the high point to the north, which is just north of the Summit House and reached via the Crystal Mountain Express Lift.

events.note: Register and firelookout.com date a National Park Service cab to 1934. Willhite (2016 visit) does not believe a lookout existed on this site.
Registered May 26, 2012 as FFLOS US 1274, WA 174

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com give a 1934 NPS cab; Willhite, after a 2016 visit, does not believe a lookout existed on this site and attributes the details to Crystal Peak. Not resolved. The story gives both.
The register and the Forest Lookouts site place it in Mount Rainier National Park; Willhite says Crystal Mountain is outside the park. Not resolved.
The register gives 6,605 feet (2,013 m); Willhite says that is a 1945 map figure at the claimed lookout point and gives the summit as 6,840 feet.

notes_for_editor: Existence is disputed. FFLOS and firelookout.com give an NPS cab built 1934 and gone in the 1970s, but Willhite's 2016 visit (no footings found; he doubts it existed) is a direct challenge, and he ties the details to Crystal Peak (see us-wa-crystal-peak). Agency NPS and the in-park location are from the register and Forest Lookouts; Willhite disputes the location. Record elevation_m 2013.2 matches the 6,605 ft figure that Willhite calls a 1945 map value; no correction proposed because the register itself gives that figure. The access level 'restricted' (seasonal) rests on Willhite's summer gondola route, not on the ski-area setting; no source states the resort's access policy, so an editor may want to change it. Used 1 WebSearch, 5 page reads, and 1 grep read of the Forest Lookouts page. Staffing and fire history are absent from every source read.
